title: SDK graceful failure contract and example snippets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: SDK consumers report confusion when streaming or long-running requests fail mid-flight. Current SDKs return opaque maps or throw language-specific exceptions with inconsistent fields (sometimes message-only, sometimes nested). This leads to duplicated application retry logic, inconsistent telemetry, and a poor developer experience.

Goal: Define a lightweight, language-idiomatic "graceful failure" contract across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs that: 1) standardizes a minimal error surface (code, retriable, safe_to_resume, http_status, hint), 2) provides clear actionable messages and sample snippets for common failure modes, 3) includes a small adapter layer in each SDK for translations to/from runtime errors, and 4) documents streaming resume semantics with examples (resume token, resume-after-offset).

Design summary (high level):
- Error surface: canonical fields: code (string), message (string), retriable (boolean), resume_token (optional string), retry_after_seconds (optional int), sdk_hint (optional string), docs_url (optional string), rpc_status (optional int). Each SDK will expose a typed Error class/struct with these fields, plus a to_protocol() / from_protocol() translator to map service payloads and transport errors.
- Streaming behaviour: define three terminal states for streams (Complete, TransientFailure, TerminalFailure). TransientFailure surfaces resume_token when safe, and SDK helpers will offer a resume() convenience that replays state and appends missing messages. TerminalFailure will expose a human-friendly hint and docs_url.
- Retry guidance: include a standardized retry metadata blob (retry_after_seconds, jitter_hint, idempotency_hint) and examples for exponential/backoff with maximum total budget.
- Migration: provide a short migration guide for existing customers (v1->v2): map old exception fields to new ones, quick patch in TypeScript and Python (try/except wrapper) and a Go middleware example.

Acceptance criteria:
- One language-idiomatic Error type implemented in Python, TS, and Go with translation layer for runtime error payloads.
- Streaming resume helper implemented in each SDK with at least one unit + integration test against replay fixture.
- Examples in docs for three common cases: transient network interruption, token-quota denial with retry_after, and model fallback decision.
- Migration guide and changelog entry.
- Telemetry emitted on error construction with labels: sdk_language, error_code, retriable (true/false), resumed (true/false).
- Internal PRs for each SDK and a final umbrella PR linking the design doc.

Deliverables:
- Confluence design page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/Graceful+Failure+Contract (draft)
- Python PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/1123 (WIP)
- TypeScript PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/905 (draft)
- Go PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/344 (planned)
- Docs page + migration guide under /docs/errors/graceful-failure.md

Notes on trade-offs:
- Keep error surface intentionally small to avoid SDK churn; prefer optional hint fields for future expansion.
- Avoid embedding full stack traces in the canonical error object; offer a separate debug metadata channel for internal telemetry.
- Resumability will be conservative: only allow resume when resume_token present and server indicates resume-safe to prevent semantic corruption of stateful streams.

Testing approach: unit tests for Error construction and serialization, integration tests against a local replay test server that can simulate mid-stream failures and provide resume_tokens, and a small e2e test that verifies telemetry tags emitted on error creation.

Rollout plan: ship as opt-in beta flag in SDK minor releases; enable for customers who opt in via feature flag. After 6 weeks of telemetry and no regressions, flip default on and publish migration guidance.
